publications.assertionSummary: Land highlight: 'frontier allotments at Billerica and Mendon'; body: 'a frontier interest among the proprietors of Mendon.'

incoming.explanation: The Mendon allotment is the second leg of the frontier-rights pattern.
The 1667 incorporation versus the 1662/3 death qualifies how John's name in the Mendon proprietors' record should be read - a right carried forward or retrospective, not proof of settlement.
Distinguishes the post-1667 son's and widow's Mendon proprietary lots from John Sr.'s own pre-incorporation 1662 Mendon allotment.

shortLabel: Ballou - John among Braintree men allotted at Mendon, 1662

sources.locator: History of the Town of Milford (1882), pp. 27-35

statement: Adin Ballou's History of Milford places John Gurney among the Braintree men accepted to allotments at the new Mendon (Nipmug) plantation in 1662.
